Clipart KoreaKorean retail investors' overseas investment is once again rising rapidly as the domestic stock market's slump drags on, according to foreign media analysis.Funds Tilting Back Toward U.S. MarketsAccording to Reuters on the 8th, individual investors net purchased $4.6 billion worth of U.S. stocks last month. This far exceeds the average monthly net purchase of $2.7 billion last year.The buying continued into this month, with an estimated $600 million purchased. By stock, Amazon topped the list at $176,206,869, followed by Micron ($161,439,812) and SanDisk ($111,035,764).Reuters reported that Korean retail investors' purchases of U.S. stocks last month exceeded their purchases of domestic stocks for the first time since February. It interpreted this as illustrating how quickly individuals' confidence in the domestic stock market has weakened.Indeed, the total balance of the Return to Investment Account (RIA), created to encourage Korean retail investors to return home, stood at 2.1214 trillion won as of the 31st of last month, down 526.8 billion won from the previous month. This is the first monthly decline in the balance since its launch in March.Semiconductor Weakness Compounded by the Won VariableReuters cited Korea's strong tendency to be swayed by the earnings of major export companies as the background for individuals' preference for the U.S. stock market.This year, the KOSPI surged on the back of the AI boom, and the trend appeared to shift briefly as government tax incentives and corporate governance reforms combined, but as the weakness continued for weeks, individual investors' patience ran out, Reuters explained.On the 7th, the KOSPI closed at 6,258.77, about 33% below the intraday high recorded on June 19. It marked seven consecutive weeks of decline from the fourth week of June, and last month it plunged 22.1%, recording the third-largest monthly drop in history.This decline was largely driven by a sharp contraction in investor sentiment toward semiconductor stocks, due to doubts about the sustainability of AI investment and the pursuit by Chinese companies. In particular, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix alone accounted for 76% of the decline in market capitalization.By contrast, the S&P 500 index closed at 7,757.64 on the 7th, setting a new closing high, and the Nasdaq index also came close to its record high.Bank of America stated in a report, "We are concerned that if Korean stocks continue to underperform U.S. stocks, an outflow of overseas funds from domestic retail investors could reappear."#KOSPI#RetailInvestors#USStocks#KoreaMarkets#SamsungElectronics#SKhynix#CapitalOutflowCompanies in this storySK hynix000660.KS · SemiconductorAI KEY Company Analysis →Samsung Electronics005930.KS · SemiconductorAI KEY Company Analysis →Original reporting by Kang Ji-won for Seoul Economic Daily.AI-translated from Korean.
